text:
Anya: quick sync — we need to lock order for Optimize toolkit features. My strawman: 1) batching improvements (short-term perf + low infra risk), 2) prefix/KV caching (mid-term, some infra work), 3) quantization profiles + auto-quantizer (big win but high risk). Putting quant last lets us ship quick wins and measure impact. RICE notes below. Thoughts?

Mike: for Dedicated customers latency is priority. If quant saves 2-3x cost but increases 10-20ms p99, that trade matters. Do we have a SLA/latency knob to compensate?

Jesse: quant integration needs evaluation. Two risks: 1) accuracy regressions on handlers (we need eval harness), 2) inference runtime changes (kernel selection). We should do a 2-week spike to validate delta on 1–2 representative models.

Tom: customers A and B explicitly asked for smaller token cost (quant) — but they also flag latency. they'd accept small latency if cost delta is large. So customer asks pull towards quant earlier.

Ravi: propose split approach: ship batching + cache first, and simultaneously run a quant spike and small beta with a risk-controlled rollout. That buys time and appeases customers.

Anya: ok proposal: ship batching Q1 (MVP = dynamic grouping + per-request batching config), caching Q2 (prefix + KV), run quant spike in parallel with an internal beta for selected customers. If spike passes eval gates, we can reprioritize to fast-track quant.

Jesse: agree. Spike plan (rough):
```
- select 2 models (chat, embed)
- baseline perf & quality (eval suite)
- try static 8-bit + QAT-lite
- measure p50/p95/p99 & eval regression on prompts
- report with go/no-go thresholds
```

Mike: small ask — include a latency SLO fallback in rollout (route to non-quant model if p99 > threshold). We have routing infra for fallback already.

Anya: noted. I'll add rollout policy: canary -> region rollout -> fallback route.

Tom: from CS, I can line up 2 customers for beta (A, B). They want cost estimates. Can we give rough numbers?

Jesse: rough back-of-envelope: static 8-bit may reduce token cost 2x-3x depending on ops; embedding models less deterministic. We'll quantify in spike.

Anya: decision check: do we all agree to ship batching first, caching second, and run quant spike in parallel with an option to re-order if spike clears gates? React with :thumbsup: if yes, :thumbsdown: if not.
